case_title: Ansar Ahmad v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr.
previous_criminal_record: Yes, both respondents have chequered criminal record
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.147, s.148, s.149, s.307, s.120-B, s.34; Explosive Substances Act s.3, s.4
aggravating_circumstances: Contract killing, criminal record of respondents, motive related to witness status
neutral_facts: The accused, along with his son and companions, were present in front of a bank when the accused Vanshraj Yadav attacked the accused Ashfaque Ahmad by throwing a grenade. Subsequently, other accused persons started indiscriminate firing, resulting in the death of Ashfaque Ahmad on the spot and injuries to Razi Ahmad. Two accused persons were caught at the scene, and weapons, including a grenade, pistols, magazines, and a mobile phone, were recovered from their possession. One of the accused disclosed that the respondent Rajesh Vikram Singh and his brother had sent the accused persons to commit the murder of Ashfaque Ahmad. The motive was that the father-in-law of Ashfaque Ahmad was a witness in another criminal case against Rajesh Vikram Singh, in which he was eventually convicted. The High Court granted bail to the respondents, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, finding that the High Court did not consider relevant material, including the criminal records of the respondents, the nature of the crime, and the presence of crucial eye witnesses.
